chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, raising it (as a marfu' narration) to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), said:

A man came to him at al-Kufa and said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have committed adultery, so purify me.' He said: 'From where are you?' He said: 'From Muzayna.' He said: 'Do you recite anything from the Quran?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then recite.' He recited and recited well. He said: 'Are you afflicted with madness?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then go away until we inquire about you.' So the man went away.

Then he returned to him afterwards and said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I have committed adultery, so purify me.' So he said: 'Do you have a wife?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Is she residing with you in the city?' He said: 'Yes.' So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered him and said: 'Go away until we inquire about you.' So he sent someone to his people and asked about his situation. They said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! He is of sound mind.'

So he returned to him the third time and said to him the same as before. He said to him: 'Go away until we inquire about you.' So he returned to him the fourth time. When he confessed, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to Qanbar: 'Keep him detained.' Then he became displeased, then said: 'How ugly it is for a man among you to commit one of these acts of immorality and then disgrace himself before the leaders of the community! Could he not have repented in his own home? By Allah, his repentance between himself and Allah is superior to my establishing the hadd penalty upon him.'

Then he brought him out and called among the people: 'O community of Muslims! Come out so that the hadd penalty may be established upon this man, and let none of you recognize his companion.' So he brought him to the open ground. He said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! Give me respite to pray two rak'ahs (cycles of prayer).' Then he placed him in his pit and faced the people. He said: 'O community of Muslims! This is a right from the rights of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic! So whoever has upon his neck a right owed to Allah, let him depart; and he should not establish the penalties of Allah, the one upon whose neck is a hadd owed to Allah.'

So the people dispersed and there remained only he and al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He took a stone and proclaimed Allah's greatness three times, then pelted him with three stones, with three proclamations for each stone. Then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) pelted him just as Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) had done. Then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) pelted him. So the man died. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) brought him out, ordered a grave to be dug for him, prayed over him, and buried him. It was said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! Will you not wash him?' So he said: 'He has been washed by that which purifies him until the Day of Resurrection. He was patient in a grievous matter.'

key_terms.التوبة: Repentance — the Imam emphasized private repentance as spiritually superior to public punishment
key_terms.الجبان: Al-Jabban — an open ground or cemetery area outside the city, used for executions
key_terms.الحد/الحدود: Hadd/Hudud — Quranic prescribed penalties for specific offenses
key_terms.الزنا: Zina — unlawful sexual intercourse, one of the major sins with a prescribed penalty (hadd)
key_terms.طَهِّرْنِي: 'Purify me' — the man's request for the hadd to be applied as an act of purification from sin
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — epithet for Allah
key_terms.قنبر: Qanbar — the loyal servant and companion of Imam Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) administer the hadd penalty for zina in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a detailed historical account of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) administering the hadd penalty for zina (adultery) in Kufa. The Imam demonstrated great care in verifying the man's mental competence and sanity before accepting his confession, requiring four separate voluntary confessions — a requirement established in Islamic jurisprudence — while also expressing that sincere private repentance is superior to public punishment. The account illustrates the Imam's mercy alongside strict adherence to divine law, his instruction that those who have pending sins upon them should not participate in executing punishment, and his final statement that the man's patient endurance of the hadd purified him until the Day of Resurrection.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) raising it to Amir Al-Momineenasws, said, ‘A man came over to himasws at Al-Kufa, so he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! I had committed adultery, so purify me’. Heasws said: ‘From where are you (coming from)?’ He said, ‘From Muzeyna’. Heasws said: ‘Have you read anything from the Quran?’ He said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘So read’. So he read, and it was good (recitation). So heasws said: ‘Are you with insanity’. He said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘So go away, until we ask about you’. So the man went away. Then he returned to himasws afterwards, so he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! I have committed adultery, so purify me’. So heasws said: ‘Is there a wife for you?’ He said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Is she staying with you in the city?’ He said, ‘Yes’. So Amir Al-Momineenasws ordered him, So go away until we ask about you’. So he sent someone to his people who asked about his news. So they said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! He is of correct mind’. So he returned to him for the third time, and he said to him similar to his words before. So heasws said to him: ‘Go away until we ask about you’. So he returned to him for the fourth time. So when he confessed, Amir Al-Momineenasws said to Qanbar: ‘Keep him locked up’. Then heasws got annoyed, then said: ‘There is nothing more uglier with the man from you that he comes to one of these immoralities, so he disgraces himself upon the chiefs of the tribes. Why did he not repent in his own house, for by Allahazwj, his repentance between him and Allahazwj is superior than myasws establishing the Penalty (Hadd) upon him’. And he called out among the people: ‘O group of the Muslims! Come out for the establishment of the Penalty (Hadd) upon this man, and not one of you should be able to recognise his companion’. So heasws brought him out to the wilderness. So he said, ‘Respite me, O Amir Al-Momineenasws, while I Pray two cycles’. Then heasws placed him in his pit, and the people faced him. So heasws said: ‘O group of the Muslims! This is a right from the Rights of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic! So the one whom had (such) a right upon his own neck, so let him disperse, and he should not establish the Penalties of Allahazwj, the one on whose neck is due a Penalty (Hadd) of Allahazwj’. So the people dispersed and there remained himselfasws, and Al-Hassanasws and Al-Husaynasws. So heasws grabbed the stones, exclaimed the Greatness of Allahazwj with three exclamations, then pelted him with three stones, during each stone, three exclamations. Then Al-Hassanasws pelted him similarly to what Amir Al-Momineenasws had pelted him. Then Al-Husaynasws pelted himasws. So the man died, and Amir Al-Momineenasws brought him out. So heasws ordered for a grave to be dug out for him, and Prayed over him, and buried him. So it was said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! Will you not wash him (before burying him)?’ So heasws said: ‘He has been washed by what has purified him up to the Day of Judgement. He was patient upon a grievous matter’.
